Ndamba

The football app with purpose: drills, sessions and the training week, matches tagged live with the Njangi Index, video, each player's journey, two books and a football game, from U8 to the first team.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem

Possession percentages say little about how a team really plays. Many coaches in neighbourhoods and academies plan sessions on paper and remember a match instead of measuring it, and a club rarely keeps the same game model and the same words from U8 to the first team.

02

What it does

Ndamba carries one method, the Njangi Code: possession with purpose, where the ball goes round the whole team like the pot of a njangi. Coaches find its 64 drills with their diagrams, build sessions, and plan the week by days counted from the match, from MD-4 to MD-1, with the load on a chart. During a match they tag it from the touchline, one tap per action; the app turns the tags into the Njangi Index out of 100, five sub-indices, a summary of how the team played and objectives for the next week. Video analysis, a player space with each player's week, load and journey, and Mola, an agent that prepares work inside the app, complete it. The coaching book and the first novel of the Lionceaux saga can be read in the app, and Lionceaux Football, a neighbourhood football game, opens on its own page.

03

How it is built

React and TypeScript, hosted on Vercel. The team, sessions, matches and tags are kept in the browser on the device (IndexedDB), so live tagging keeps working with no network and the screen stays awake. Mola runs on a built-in engine and can call the Claude API through a server function; a WhatsApp message, an e-mail or a calendar file always waits for approval. One JSON description draws each pitch diagram the same way in the books and in the app. Lionceaux Football is a Unity web build of about 25 MB on its own page, lighter on phones.
